Barotrauma is a very fun game to play with friends. The different roles you can play are all well-distinguished from one another and I like that you can still fulfil parts of different roles than your main role. The game has a very high skill floor, though. You can’t really play without having done the tutorials for every role and even then I keep getting my ass beat on 15% difficulty. There are a bunch of advanced settings you can toggle on and off so there’s a lot of modifiers for higher skilled players to mess around with. I like that there’s a lot of different mission types as well as a campaign I have yet to complete. Things can get a bit stressful, though. Overall this is a great game to play with some friends if you are willing to put in the effort to learn the game and its mechanics!

One of the best 2d coop survival horror games that is out there right now.

The amout of fun and unique situations you can have in this game are endless and there is always something new to see.
For example, every mission you do, will always have a different outcome and might end in a big disaster.
A small cargo transport from A to B, might also end in your submarine getting sandwich'd by 6 hammerheads.

The game itself is kinda easy to understand and the tutorial explains all the basics that you need to know, but the deeper you get with your class, the harder it gets to master it.

I would recommend to play it with a nice crew of friends or people that you trust with to be in a "kinda" unstable submarine in the deep seas of Europe.
Otherwise, good luck out there with nothing left than one room full of oxygen because "somehow" the room without any explosive components exploded.

The amout of content gets more and more with every update and the developers are always providing sneakpeeks and updates to the community.
From what it was on its Steam release and what it is now, it has come a great way.

Good luck surviving out there!!!

2025 updated review after a two year break:

I would say that the game is really solid in its current state. I can't comment on regular multiplayer nor singleplayer, but when playing in coop with friends it's a blast.
Our latest campaign started off entirely vanilla (to see the changes more clear), and it got plenty of content. Especially with the addition of colony-missions for a bit of variety. I also got pleasantly surprised by the upgraded enviromental graphics; some nice parallax effects etc.

If you enjoy games that rewards good teamwork with friends this is a easy pick, and somewhat of a no-brainer when on sale. It's super easy to whip up a campaign, or even just a sandbox for your friends to join and play over a few weeks.

Regarding regular multiplayer, it's a hit or miss depending on the crew. It traditionally ranges from total chaos to organised chaos, but also adds stuff like potential traitors etc. That said, I have had a few really nice sessions on random servers as well.

I also want to mention the incredibly talented modding community, as well as all the great submarines on the workshop. Whenever you get tired of the vanilla stuff, there is a never ending supply of itempacks and stuff to choose from.
its fun, but only if you can find cool people to play it with. The Offical Discord can probably set you up with that.

A long time ago, I was playing on a casual Missions-oriented server with Traitors enabled. Back then, there were only a handful of traitor missions to complete, so as long as you knew what to look for, you could catch a traitor pretty easily.

Well, one game I was a security guard, and I found some guy swapping out the oxygen in our diving masks with welding fuel. Textbook traitor. I immediately started beating the fear of god into the sailor (though he certainly did protest against it) and slapped some cuffs onto his crumpled and unconscious form. Now, the issue was how to "deal" with the traitor.

Lesser men may have decided to simply keep the poor man locked in his cuffs and weld him into the crew quarters. With such damning evidence, you would certainly not be keeping an innocent sailor from performing his duties. However, I wanted to make a statement...

In front of a handful of other sailors who had gathered to watch the spectacle, I ordered the engineer to disconnect and rewire the ballast tank pump so as not to pump water out of the ship, but instead slowly pump water in. I placed the traitor into the ballast tank, water already knee high, and then climbed out.

After a minute or two, all the commotion from beneath the hatch had finally ceased. Lets just say that the other sailors got the message.

I Love this game. Does it have issues, heck yeah it does. However, after all this time has passed since it released and since I started playing it, I still love to play it. The developers are still updating it and the modding community for this game has always been extraordinary. Much like other comfort games if mine, I imagine I'll be returning to this game every once in a while, for a long time to come.
If you have pals, buy it. If you are one of the many lonely gamers, don't. Do not play random lobbies. It's a great teambuilding exercise with insanely memorable moments.

Then the ship was flooded and invaded by crawlers.

A crew mate mistook a green flare for a leak in the nuclear reactor.

We had previously bought fuel rods but for a reason they were not on board the submarine. Slowly the power ran out and we drifted in the middle of the ocean. Next the oxygen wore out and we need breathing masks. We are fucked.

I suggest playing with friends because online matches can be quite chaotic and nonsensical ( wich is part of the fun also ) but other than that , playing solo is viable.

Takes a little bit to learn but it has a job role tailored to that experience. Modding support is super nice but the base game is honestly good enough without it. Better with friends but single player is very well done if you go that route.

So much room to make your own fun... And if you enjoy customization and building subs like me, you'll really love the editor provided. Ive spent more time making and tweaking subs then playing.

This game is best experienced in MP. There are many MP servers up and a very active modding community. Single player is starting to get some love however and the bot AI is starting to improve. They even have an unstable branch available for players to test the upcoming features.

There can be a lot to learn when starting some roles but once you understand the basics it's easy to pickup and play. I also kind of love the paper cutout pinwheel style art. It can definitely be a bit janky sometimes but this game has so much room to grow.

Can't wait until medical gets really flushed out and we can give people thresher face hands.
